standards_review.notes: git-workflow.md requires '<type>: <short description>' with no scope; anti-patterns section explicitly forbids scope notation. 4 commits violate this: 'test(EPMCDME-14505): add Windows Sandbox smoke-test scripts', 'feat(EPMCDME-14505): add check_handshake_state IPC command', 'feat(EPMCDME-14505): add verify_download and refactor download_file', 'refactor(EPMCDME-14505): delete six-layer acquisition flow'. 1 additional commit has no valid conventional type at all: 'EPMCDME-14573-windows-node-shim-runner-path: add planning artifacts' uses a branch slug in place of the type field.
.ai-run/guides/standards/code-quality.md is absent from the repo; no standard to adjudicate against

.ai-run/guides/development/security-patterns.md is absent from the repo; two concrete defects found regardless: (1) src-tauri/src/commands/downloader.rs:78 calls verify_download with expected_hash=None on every download_file invocation so downloaded binaries are written to disk without SHA-256 integrity verification; (2) src-tauri/src/commands/downloader.rs:79 writes the caller-supplied dest path via tokio::fs::write without any prefix validation, enabling path traversal to arbitrary writable locations if the renderer is compromised

blocking_findings.location: commits: 'test(EPMCDME-14505): add Windows Sandbox smoke-test scripts', 'feat(EPMCDME-14505): add check_handshake_state IPC command', 'feat(EPMCDME-14505): add verify_download and refactor download_file', 'refactor(EPMCDME-14505): delete six-layer acquisition flow'
blocking_findings.violation: git-workflow.md anti-patterns section forbids scope notation ('feat(auth): ...' style) and requires plain '<type>: <description>'; all four commits use '(EPMCDME-14505)' as a scope suffix on the type
blocking_findings.why_blocking: documented anti-pattern in the commit-format standard; the guide explicitly names this form as something to avoid in favour of the scope-free format
blocking_findings.remedy: reword each subject to drop the parenthesised scope: 'test: add Windows Sandbox smoke-test scripts', 'feat: add check_handshake_state IPC command', 'feat: add verify_download and refactor download_file', 'refactor: delete six-layer acquisition flow'

blocking_findings.violation: git-workflow.md requires the format '<type>: <description>' where type is one of feat|fix|docs|test|chore|refactor; this subject uses a branch slug as the type token, which matches none of the allowed types
blocking_findings.why_blocking: the commit carries no recognised conventional type; it does not conform to the documented commit-format standard
blocking_findings.remedy: reword to 'chore: EPMCDME-14573 windows node shim runner path — add planning artifacts' or 'docs: EPMCDME-14573 planning artifacts'

blocking_findings.violation: verify_download is always invoked with expected_hash=None; the SHA-256 verification path is implemented but the download_file command never supplies a hash, so every downloaded binary is accepted regardless of content
blocking_findings.why_blocking: files written here are executable binaries installed on end-user machines; omitting integrity verification leaves the install path open to MITM or CDN substitution without detection
blocking_findings.remedy: add an optional expected_sha256: Option<String> parameter to download_file and forward it into verify_download; callers that know the expected hash get verification; callers that do not pass None and accept the risk explicitly

blocking_findings.violation: tokio::fs::write(&dest, &bytes) writes to the caller-supplied dest path with no prefix validation; dest arrives directly from the IPC call as a String and is not constrained to any app-owned directory
blocking_findings.why_blocking: a compromised renderer or injected IPC message can write arbitrary byte content to any path writable by the process, including system directories and per-user startup items
blocking_findings.remedy: resolve dest against a known safe root (e.g. app_data_dir() or a temporary directory) and verify the canonical result remains within that root before writing; return an error for paths that escape the allowed prefix
